scams.name: Maya Bay National Park Fee Double-Billing
scams.description:
You pay ฿1,800 for a speedboat day tour to Maya Bay from Ao Nang. At the Maya Bay entry point, the operator demands an additional ฿400 'national park entrance fee.' The legitimate Hat Noppharat Thara–Mu Koh Phi Phi National Park foreigner fee is ฿400 — but scam operators pocket this AND don't remit it to the park, effectively charging tourists twice if the park fee was already bundled.

The Thai government's 10x foreigner pricing creates the structural space for the scam — Thais pay ฿40, foreigners pay ฿400 for the same entry, so operators exploit the differential with opaque billing. One traveler thread elaborates: 'It's not a scam in the sense that it's legal and you have to pay to enter national parks, but the fact that there's such a massive markup…' — meaning the fee is legitimate but operators often bundle-unbundle to charge both.

The parallel Phi Phi scam is the ferry-ticket switcheroo. One report documents: 'We got tricked into paying the ferry for Krabi when we asked specifically for Ao…' Tourists are sold a 'Phi Phi → Ao Nang' ticket that turns out to be 'Phi Phi → Krabi Town,' requiring another ฿300–฿500 leg. The defensive move is to book Maya Bay tours through Klook or 12go.asia with the park fee explicitly listed as 'included' in the voucher, and use Chao Koh Ferry or Songserm directly for ferries — avoid booth middlemen. Tourist Police: 1155.
scams.avoidance: Book Maya Bay tours on Klook or 12go.asia with 'park fee included' explicitly stated Bring ฿400 cash per person as backup — if the tour says included, you have protection against re-billing For Phi Phi ferries, book directly with Chao Koh Ferry (chaokohferryphiphi.com) or Songserm — not booth middlemen Confirm your ferry ticket destination in writing: 'Phi Phi → Ao Nang' vs. 'Phi Phi → Krabi Town' (different piers, different fees) Keep printed vouchers on you; operators occasionally try to double-bill even on prepaid tours
scams.location: Maya Bay (on Phi Phi Leh), tour operator pickups from Phi Phi Don and Ao Nang
scams.tldr: A ฿1,800 Maya Bay speedboat tour from Ao Nang demands a ฿400 'national park fee' at the entry — but the fee was already bundled in the ticket and scam operators pocket the second charge without remitting to the park, exploiting the 10x foreigner-pricing differential.

scams.name: Phi Phi 'Bucket' Drink Spiking & Watered Cocktails
scams.description:
It's party night on Loh Dalum Beach and a beach bar sells ฿300 buckets of 'rum and coke' — a plastic sandcastle-style bucket with spirits, Red Bull, mixer. You drink two and wake up in your hostel with no memory of 3–4 hours and ฿8,000 missing. Traveler reports document the pattern directly: 'I walk into the bar and immediately knew that I walked into a scam… I was drunk (rum and pineapple served in a BUCKET) at Phi Phi…'

The Phi Phi bucket is a known delivery vehicle for drink-spiking — spirits are mixed out of sight, benzodiazepines or GHB dissolve quickly in sugary cocktails, and the small plastic cups within the bucket prevent monitoring individual drinks. The related scam is watered-down or entirely fake spirits: bottles behind the bar contain half-strength vodka or gin cut with water; popular spirits (Jägermeister, Malibu) are refilled with cheap substitutes. The damage is financial (฿150 for a ฿20-worth drink) and health (unknown-provenance alcohol).

Phi Phi has a grim 2025 safety record. Khaosod English July 2025 'French Tourist Dies at Phi Phi Police Station After Heavy Drinking' and Thaiger November 2025 'Canadian tourist drowns after losing consciousness at Koh Phi Phi' both occurred with alcohol as a factor. BBC March 2025 covered a boat fire that left a British tourist missing. The defensive rules are absolute: no buckets ever, no drinks left unattended, travel in groups, and keep most cash and cards in your hotel safe. Phi Phi is walk-only (no cars), so Grab is not a rescue option — trust networks and group accountability matter more. Tourist Police: 1155.
scams.avoidance: Never accept a bucket cocktail on Phi Phi — order bottled beer or cocktails mixed in front of you Watch your drink being made and keep it in your hand; discard any drink you set down Travel in groups; Phi Phi is walk-only and solo rescue options are limited Store passport, extra cards, and most cash at your accommodation; carry only ฿1,000–฿2,000 and one card If you feel suddenly drunk beyond your drinks, head to your hotel immediately and contact your accommodation's night staff
scams.location: Tonsai Village bars, Loh Dalum Beach parties, Sunflower Bar, Slinky Bar
scams.tldr: A Loh Dalum beach bar sells ฿300 'rum and coke' buckets — a known delivery vehicle for drink-spiking with benzos or GHB, with documented 2025 tourist deaths (French tourist July 2025, Canadian drowning November 2025) directly linked to bucket consumption.

scams.name: Phi Phi Ferry Middleman Ticket Markup
scams.description:
You walk to a beach-front ferry booth in Ao Nang and buy a Phi Phi return for ฿1,400. At the pier you see tourists boarding the same ferry with tickets from Chao Koh Ferry or Songserm for ฿800. The booth you used was a middleman reseller, not the ferry company. One thread notes: 'It's not a scam, they are a travel agent and provide you with a service at a commission. It's no different than the 1,000,000 of travel agents kiosks you can…' — technically legal, but 50–75% markup on publicly-priced ferry tickets.

The more aggressive variant is the destination switcheroo. The ticket says 'Krabi Province' in small print, which legally covers both Ao Nang and Krabi Town. Tourists assuming they're going back to their Ao Nang hotel arrive at Krabi Town's Klong Chilad pier instead — 35 km from Ao Nang and a ฿300–฿500 taxi or songthaew leg away.

A safety variant matters on Phi Phi routes: monsoon-season speedboat trips are dangerous. One traveler warns: 'A speed boat during monsoon is not advisable. Larger ferry at minimum but check Windy before stepping on a boat.' BBC's 2025 coverage of the Koh Tao boat fire and Thaiger's November 2025 Phi Phi drowning both relate to unlicensed/unsafe boat operations. The defensive move is to book directly with Chao Koh Ferry (chaokohferryphiphi.com), Songserm, or Phi Phi Cruiser at their official sites, specify destination precisely in writing ('Ao Nang beach pier' not just 'Krabi'), and never board a speedboat in rough monsoon conditions. Tourist Police: 1155.
scams.avoidance: Book Phi Phi ferries directly with Chao Koh Ferry (chaokohferryphiphi.com), Songserm, or Phi Phi Cruiser on their official sites Specify destination precisely in writing: 'Ao Nang beach pier' (not just 'Krabi') During monsoon (May–October), take the larger ferry over speedboats; check Windy for wave conditions before boarding Pay by credit card where possible — chargebacks resolve fly-by-night booking booth disputes Keep the printed voucher and compare to the actual ferry company's schedule on arrival
scams.location: Ao Nang beach pier, Rassada Pier (Phuket), Krabi Town Klong Chilad pier, Phi Phi Tonsai pier
scams.tldr: A beach-front Ao Nang booth sells a Phi Phi return for ฿1,400 — the direct Chao Koh Ferry or Songserm rate is ฿800, the booth is a middleman reseller, and the destination switcheroo lands you at Krabi Town pier instead of Ao Nang.

scams.name: Tonsai Village Luggage Porter Overcharge
scams.description:
You arrive at Phi Phi's Tonsai Pier. A porter with a cart offers to carry your luggage to your hotel — '฿100 baht' (you hear). At the hotel he demands ฿500 per bag. Phi Phi is walk-only (no cars, no tuk-tuks), which makes porters genuinely useful — but the pricing is opaque and tourist-padded. Standard rate is ฿50–฿100 per bag for short hotel transfers; ฿300+ per bag is aggressive upcharging.

The parallel Phi Phi transport scam is the long-tail boat overcharge. One thread notes: 'We rented a long boat/driver for the day in phiphi and it was well worth it. I can't remember the price but it was cheap.' Fair private long-tail for a full day is ฿2,500–฿3,500 total (not per person); tourist pricing hits ฿6,000+. For short transfers (Tonsai → Long Beach), ฿200–฿300 per group is fair; ฿800+ is scam pricing.

Phi Phi is small enough that most hotels are 5–15 minutes walk from Tonsai Pier, so a porter isn't strictly necessary if you can roll a bag over the boardwalk. The defensive move is to agree on the price in writing before handing over bags ('฿100 per bag, total ฿200 for two bags'), confirm 'total' vs 'per bag' explicitly, and pay on arrival — not before. For long-tail boats, negotiate the rate for the group (not per person) and have the driver write the price on paper. These are low-stakes scams (฿200–฿1,000 per incident) but universally targeted at fresh-off-the-ferry tourists. Tourist Police: 1155.
scams.avoidance: Agree on price in writing on your phone before handing over bags: '100 baht per bag, 2 bags, 200 baht total' Know benchmarks: porter ฿50–฿100 per bag short transfer; long-tail Tonsai → Long Beach ฿200–฿300 per group; full-day private long-tail ฿2,500–฿3,500 per boat Most Tonsai hotels are 5–15 min walk from pier — you may not need a porter Pay on arrival, not before — this maintains negotiation leverage Photograph the porter's tag or boat license number so you have accountability
scams.location: Phi Phi Tonsai Pier, Tonsai Village walking paths, Long Beach trail
scams.tldr: A Tonsai Pier porter offers '฿100' to carry your bags to your hotel — at the door he demands ฿500 per bag. The fair rate is ฿50–฿100 per bag for short hotel transfers, and the parallel long-tail boat racket runs ฿6,000+ for trips that should cost ฿2,500–฿3,500.

scams.name: Phi Phi Accommodation Over-Booking & 'Upgrade' Fee
scams.description:
You arrive at your Phi Phi hostel with a printed Booking.com confirmation. The clerk says: 'Sorry, we overbooked, but we have a better room in our other property for ฿500 extra per night.' The 'other property' is a different bungalow with a worse bed and no Booking.com paper trail. One traveler thread: 'Contacted Agoda and once they had clarified it with the hotel they gave me a full refund within a week or so.' The scam depends on you accepting the 'upgrade' on the spot without contacting the platform.

Phi Phi's peak season (December–February, plus Full Moon weeks on nearby Phangan that spill over) creates structural over-booking pressure. Operators accept bookings beyond capacity, then reshuffle tourists to whichever unit is least profitable. The 'upgrade' framing is the disguise — it converts a bait-and-switch into an apparent value-add.

The defensive move is to never accept an 'upgrade' on the spot — contact Booking.com, Agoda, or Airbnb support immediately via in-app chat; they will typically provide either a full refund or force the hotel to honor the original booking. If physically denied the original room, stay at the alternative for one night only (document everything) and dispute via platform + credit-card chargeback on return home. Screenshot all booking confirmations before arrival. For Phi Phi specifically, book 4+ weeks ahead for Dec–Feb and use platforms with free-cancellation windows as backup. Tourist Police: 1155.
scams.avoidance: Book through Booking.com, Agoda, or Airbnb with credit card payment and screenshot your confirmation On arrival overbooking: contact platform support immediately via in-app chat — do not accept 'upgrade' on the spot Document all communications and the actual unit condition with photos/video If forced to accept alternative, dispute via platform + credit card chargeback on return For Phi Phi peak season (Dec–Feb), book 4+ weeks ahead and use free-cancellation windows as backup
scams.location: Tonsai Village hostels, Loh Dalum beach bungalows, Long Beach resorts
scams.tldr: You arrive at a Tonsai hostel with a printed Booking.com confirmation and the clerk claims they overbooked — but a 'better room' in another property is available for ฿500 extra per night. The 'other property' is a worse bungalow with no platform paper trail.
